newsitem.title: USA: Procept antiviral gel trial results good.
newsitem.headline: Procept antiviral gel trial results good.

text.p: Procept Inc said Monday that initial review of the Phase I safety trial its PRO 2000 Gel, designed for prevention of sexually transmitted diseases, indicates the product was well tolerated in healthy female volunteers.
Procept said the product is designed to prevent of human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1) infection and other sexually transmitted diseases.

It said the double-blind study, conducted at the Institute of Tropical Medicine in Antwerp, Belgium, involved 37 healthy women who administered either PRO 2000 Gel or a placebo gel intravaginally for up to two weeks. No serious adverse events were reported, the company said. A thorough analysis of the data is under way.

Procept said laboratory studies have shown that PRO 2000 is active against a wide range of HIV strains from both the developed and developing world. It is also active against other STD pathogens, such as herpes simplex virus type 2, a cause of genital lesions that are believed to be a portal for HIV entry.
